strongest_claim: Architectural attention masks intended to enforce conditional independence (causal non-interference) between semantic goals and physical world dynamics fail silently via higher-order transformer self-attention pathways, producing goal-conditioned hallucinated dynamics under invariant actions.
why_not_generic: It is currently treated as an implementation oversight rather than a security mechanism; to elevate it, the threat must be reframed from passive observational discrepancy to active semantic side-channel injection, where adversary-perturbed goal prompts induce systemic dynamics distortion (e.g., misestimating collision boundaries or affordances) during Model Predictive Control (MPC) rollouts without altering the actor's immediate action distribution.
exact_gate: Run closed-loop MPC rollout evaluation using native LIBERO-10 benchmark tasks (e.g., `libero_spatial` suite) where the planner selects actions by evaluating trajectories against the visual world model: measure policy task completion rate (SR) drop when swapping the goal string to an adversarial distractor while keeping historical visual observations and candidate action trajectories identical, establishing whether dynamics divergence induces catastrophic rollout deviation.
defense: Strict compositional attention causal masking (blocking goal token key/value projections across all self-attention layers for both world state and intermediate action representations) or physically disentangled dual-stream backbones where the world dynamics module is computationally isolated from policy/goal embeddings.
recommendation: Do not frame this as a novel world-model security paradigm at 7-7.5 novelty in its current state. At present, this represents a bug audit of transitive attention leakage in a single open-source checkpoint. To reach top-tier novelty, demonstrate that goal-contamination in world models serves as an exploitable adversarial vector for planner hijacking or hallucinated dynamics manipulation under closed-loop execution across multiple model families.
